Photograph by Nathaniel St. Clair

On January 7, an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent fatally shot
[Renee Good](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/01/09/renee-goods-wife-
releases-statement-about-ice-shooting) in Minneapolis — a city long enriched
by immigrants and now under assault from [thousands of ICE and Customs and
Border Protection agents](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jan/13/ice-
cbp-minneapolis-teargas).

Good, a 37-year-old poet and mother of three, was driving alongside her wife,
Becca. They were observing an ICE raid in their community. “We stopped to
support our neighbors. We had whistles. They had guns,”
[said](https://www.mprnews.org/story/2026/01/09/renee-goods-wife-releases-
statement-about-ice-shooting) Becca.

Sadly, at least three other people have been killed by ICE officers in the
last five months, according to [The Marshall
Project](https://www.themarshallproject.org/2026/01/07/ice-minneapolis-
shooting-renee-good).

Among them was [Silverio Villegas
González](https://blockclubchicago.org/2025/10/20/a-tragic-homecoming/), a
38-year-old father and cook originally from Mexico, who was fatally shot
during a traffic stop in a Chicago suburb. [Keith Porter
Jr.](https://sanfernandosun.com/2026/01/07/calls-for-transparency-after-the-
fatal-shooting-of-keith-porter-jr-on-new-years-
eve/?fbclid=IwY2xjawPNFxhleHRuA2FlbQIxMABicmlkETFDMTYzMW1PaXB3VmpSb3puc3J0YwZhcHBfaWQQMjIyMDM5MTc4ODIwMDg5MgABHny7_WWBRfiv0VHU_ajMx5L6RUsP8f3WB3oDt6UOKOjH_7SBUStjRRs3a83k_aem_fHldYQhX2yCuiJp9EgHI1g),
a 43-year-old father of two — and, like Good, a U.S. citizen — was shot and
killed by an off-duty ICE agent on New Year’s Eve in Los Angeles.

While the families of all these victims await justice, the violence continues.
ICE agents have shot at least [nine people in their vehicles since
September.](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/07/us/ice-shootings-minneapolis-
other-cities.html) The Department of Homeland Security has routinely invoked
“self-defense” to justify these shootings, despite video and witnesses
repeatedly contradicting their accounts.

From Los Angeles to Washington D.C., Chicago, Memphis, New Orleans, Portland,
Charlotte, and now Minneapolis, [violence has
followed](https://www.thetrace.org/2025/12/immigration-ice-shootings-guns-
tracker/) wherever Trump has dispatched immigration agents in the name of
“public safety.”

On the same day Good was murdered, ICE conducted a [raid at a nearby
Minneapolis high school](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/minneapolis-
schools-cancel-classes-ice-raid-high-school-day-renee-nico-rcna253081),
reportedly tackling a teacher and harassing students. The next day, ICE agents
in Robbinsdale, Minnesota [forcibly detained a U.S. citizen and Red Lake
Nation descendant](https://ccxmedia.org/news/after-citizen-detained-by-ice-in-
robbinsdale-lawmakers-
respond/#:~:text=Watch%20Live-,After%20Citizen%20Detained%20By%20ICE%20in%20Robbinsdale%2C%20Lawmakers%20Respond,these%20untrained%20and%20incompetent%20agents.)
for no apparent reason. Stories of new outrages emerge almost daily.

And last fall, federal agents descended from Black Hawk helicopters in a
[midnight raid of an apartment
building](https://www.propublica.org/article/chicago-venezuela-immigration-
ice-fbi-raids-no-criminal-charges) in Chicago, [detaining all its residents,
including
children](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/mayor/press_room/press_releases/2026/january/immigration-
enforcement-suit.html). (That’s in addition to killing Villegas González — and
[shooting another person five
times](https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2025/11/20/operation-midway-
blitz-marimar-martinez-anthony-ruiz-us-supreme-court-feds-drop-case-against-
woman-shot-by-border-patrol-agent-in-brighton-park).)

This escalating violence is an outgrowth of ICE’s appalling treatment of
immigrants. Across the country, people have been rounded up, thrown in deadly
prisons, and ripped from their families — a trend that has sharply escalated
under Trump.

Thousands of masked agents in unmarked cars — equipped with [military-grade
weapons](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/oct/10/ice-immigration-
agents-military-
tactics#:~:text=Sol%C3%B3rzano%2C%20a%20Carpinteria%20city%20council,the%20grenade%20is%20disproportionately%20high.)
and the [latest surveillance technology](https://americandragnet.org/)— treat
cities like war zones while executing raids at
[workplaces](https://nebraskapublicmedia.org/en/news/news-articles/ice-raids-
push-farm-workers-to-stay-home-out-of-fear-that-could-hurt-us-food-
production/), [places of
worship](https://www.wcnc.com/article/news/local/methodist-church-ice-agents-
preschool-pickup-5-28-2025/275-0da22fdc-b8c4-45ac-8219-d6bb03b5a9ea), and
schools.

Citizens and non-citizens alike have been [racially
profiled](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/08/us/politics/supreme-court-los-
angeles-immigration.html) and [kidnapped at
courthouses](https://www.npr.org/2025/06/12/nx-s1-5409403/trump-immigration-
courts-arrests) and [off the
streets](https://immigrantjustice.org/sites/default/files/uploaded-files/no-
content-type/2025-03/164-Nava-v-DHS_Motion-to-Enforce-the-
Settlement_03-13-25.pdf?eType=EmailBlastContent&eId=1febb8fe-b0e6-4475-97cf-d178d8948dc4)
[without warrants or probable cause](https://illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/News-
Room/Current-News/001%20-%20Complaint%201.12.26.pdf?language_id=1). Trump has
also used ICE to attack free speech, abducting and jailing students like
[Mahmoud Khalil](https://www.npr.org/2025/06/23/nx-s1-5441691/mahmoud-khalil-
interview), [Mohsen Mahdawi](https://abcnews.go.com/US/mohsen-mahdawi-
columbia-student-freed-ice-feared-citizenship/story?id=121485222), and
[Rümeysa Öztürk](https://www.vanityfair.com/news/story/rumeysa-ozturk-what-i-
witnessed-inside-an-ice-womens-
prison?srsltid=AfmBOoolF5hCimMWP9Vp4-fzKcxAiy8-0OOVsCY7YV3hqrSFuruO9Sr4) who
spoke out against the Gaza genocide.

In addition to the shootings, [32 people died in ICE custody last
year](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-
interactive/2026/jan/04/ice-2025-deaths-timeline) alone — and as of this
writing, [four more people have died in
custody](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/four-migrants-die-us-ice-
custody-over-first-10-days-2026-2026-01-12/) so far this January.

Abysmal conditions in ICE prisons, including [medical
neglect](https://www.aclu.org/publications/deadly-failures-preventable-deaths-
in-us-immigrant-detention), have resulted in these tragic and avoidable
deaths, leaving families shattered and still searching for answers. [Nearly
69,000 people](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-
interactive/2025/aug/29/trump-immigration-ice-cbp-
data?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email) are currently being held in ICE
prisons, the vast majority of them [without a criminal
record](https://tracreports.org/immigration/quickfacts/). According to [
_ProPublica_ ,](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-dhs-american-
citizens-arrested-detained-against-will) ICE also detained over 170 U.S.
citizens last year.

ICE has repeatedly [denied members of Congress entry to its detention
facilities](https://www.axios.com/local/twin-cities/2026/01/10/ice-
minneapolis-ilhan-omar-denied-access), interfering with Congress’s
constitutional oversight authority. Still, Congress enables ICE’s abuses
through [billions in funding increases](https://www.brennancenter.org/our-
work/analysis-opinion/big-budget-act-creates-deportation-industrial-complex).
ICE’s $14 billion annual budget for detentions alone, note Lindsay Koshgarian
and Sarah Lazare, is [more than the total military spending of 124
countries.](https://inthesetimes.com/article/ice-immigration-chicago-trump-
broadview)

Across the country, more communities are responding to our nation’s descent
into lawlessness by uniting around our shared humanity and demanding justice.
A recent poll shows, for the first time, [net positive support — including
among self-described moderates — for abolishing
ICE](https://x.com/prem_thakker/status/2011085236696912233).

These Americans understand that no one is safe as long as ICE still exists,
operates with impunity, and terrorizes communities. How many more deaths will
it take for Congress to hold this agency accountable?
